subject: Dedicated GPU pool — invoicing cadence, prepay options, and true-up flow
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@avalontech.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@avalontech.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on Dedicated pricing structure and PO flow

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the demo last week. The execs were pleased with the throughput numbers. Before we move to an internal approval, procurement asked me to confirm a few billing items so they can scope the PO and net terms:

1) If we do an annual prepay for a dedicated GPU pool, how do true-ups work if we consume > committed throughput mid-year? Do you invoice a pro rata top-up or do you do a quarterly true-up invoice?

2) If we choose monthly billing (non-prepay) what are the guarantees? We need clear wording about throughput SLAs and burst pricing.

3) Do you accept a master PO + monthly invoices, or do you require one PO per billing period for enterprise procurement?

Can you send a simple sample invoice and an outline of the PO/net-terms flow so procurement can triage?

Cheers,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Cloud Engineering
AvalonTech

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@avalontech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated pricing structure and PO flow

Samir —

Appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise breakdown of how we typically handle each option and the pros/cons for AvalonTech. I attached a one-page sample invoice for the annual prepay and a sample PO flow.

Option A — Annual prepay (recommended for predictable heavy usage)
- Prepay covers the committed GPU pool (e.g., 32 A100-equivalent vCPUs) for 12 months.
- Discount: typically 12–20% off list depending on commit size (we can firm exact discount after sizing).
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups are standard. If you exceed committed throughput we invoice the delta at the agreed committed rate for that tier on the quarterly true-up (pro rata for the period).
- Benefits: budget predictability, lower unit price, priority capacity during regional contention.
- Invoice flow: one annual prepay invoice up-front OR split into 4 equal scheduled invoices (quarterly invoicing on prepay) if preferred. PO: master PO referencing the commitment + a single SOW is sufficient; attachments to the PO can reference the quarterly invoice schedule.

Option B — Monthly consumption billing (no prepay)
- Monthly invoice based on actual consumed tokens/throughput + baseline reserved capacity fee (if you pin a minimum pool).
- Throughput SLA: we commit to a 95th percentile latency SLO per model/route and a committed baseline throughput for the reserved pool. Bursts above baseline are allowed subject to capacity and surge pricing (explicit rates in the SOW).
- True-ups: monthly reconciliation is automatic; no true-up invoice is required beyond the month’s invoice.
- Invoice flow: master PO + monthly invoices referencing PO number is supported. Net terms (Net 30/45) are configurable by contract and standard for enterprise.

Option C — Hybrid (Annual commit + monthly metering for bursts)
- Annual commit for baseline pool with discounted rate; monthly metering charges for overages or burst capacity. We reconcile monthly and provide quarterly summaries for finance.

Key operational notes:
- Billing granularity: we invoice by committed pool SKU and metered token/second overage lines — sample invoice attached.
- True-up calculation: we look at peak sustained throughput vs committed baseline per calendar quarter and bill the difference at the committed rate scaled to the pro-rated period.
- PO acceptance: finance/legal can provide a master PO referencing the SOW; our AR team will accept a PO that references the master agreement and then accept monthly/quarterly invoices against that PO number.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Tell me which option Avalon prefers (A/B/C).
2) If you want the prepay but prefer monthly bill splits, mark that in the PO request and we’ll reflect that in the SOW.
3) If procurement needs sample legal language for SLA/true-up, I’ll loop in our legal team.

Attaching: AvalonTech_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft), Invoice_Sample_annual_prepay.xlsx

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of procurement-specific clarifications:

1) Our default is master PO + monthly invoices against that PO. Would Redwood allow the annual prepay to be referenced by a single master PO and then accept monthly invoices that draw down against the prepay? (Procurement needs a monthly invoice trail for our ERP.)

2) For quarterly true-ups, will Redwood provide a line-item breakdown (committed baseline vs overage tokens) and an early warning if we are trending > 15% above commit?

3) Net terms: Avalon's policy is Net 45. We can request Net 30 if Redwood prefers, but most vendors accept Net 45.

Please confirm and we’ll get the master PO process started.

- Procurement (on behalf of AvalonTech)

Procurement team —

We can support the exact flow you outlined: master PO referencing the annual commitment SOW + monthly invoices that draw down against the prepay balance so your ERP retains a monthly trail. Implementation notes:

- We’ll issue the annual prepay invoice when the contract is signed. If you prefer to split the prepay into 4 scheduled invoices, we can generate 4 dated invoices that draw equally against the commitment (still referenced to the master PO).
- Quarterly true-up reports: we’ll send a detailed CSV with baseline consumption, overage tokens, and per-line calculations. We’ll also enable an alert in the console to notify users once 85% of committed throughput is reached so you get an early warning (15% headroom).
- Net terms: Net 45 accepted. Please include the PO number on all invoices.

I’m looping in Marissa (finance lead) and Rishi (ops) to confirm the AR and acceptance workflow on our side.

Vanessa
